_qa_note_t20: T-20 (v0.46.0, harvest-wrapped-insight): test_archive_task_bash_assertions is NEW and is TRANSCRIBED from the 'PASS: 186' line of a real `bash .harness/scripts/test-archive-task.sh` run against the promoted archive-task.sh, never derived arithmetically (insight 2026-07-31). It read 152 when QA froze it in round 2, moved to 181 in developer round 3 and reads 186 after developer round 4; every one of those three figures was transcribed from its own run. Round 3 closed QA-1: harvest scanned only the FIRST '## Insight' heading and broke, so every later section was discarded at exit 0 with 'unaccounted lines 0' - a NEW silent-content-loss path inside K-65's own admissible class, in both twins. The fix harvests EVERY matching heading (the pre-change awk re-armed its flag on each one, so this is also the B-11 floor) and ignores a heading inside a fenced code block. 29 new bash rows: 26 across five QA-1 cases (multi-section; fenced heading; unterminated fence refuses at exit 3; a MEASURED RESIDUAL row recording that a fence INSIDE the section is still absorbed as continuation lines; and the BOUND case, a section lying entirely inside a fence, which harvests 0 entries at exit 0 and is only acceptable because the run PRINTS a 'Quoted headings: N ...' line naming every matching heading it skipped for being quoted) plus 3 in the AC-4 pre/post leg. The PS twin gained the same 26 (the AC-4 leg is bash-only by design). Developer round 4 added ONE further case per twin, 5 rows each (code-review CR-13): the TILDE half of the fence state machine had zero rows in either driver although RE_FENCE / $atReFence accept '~{3,}' and the tilde branch is not a copy of the backtick branch - a tilde opener's info string is unrestricted where a backtick opener's may hold no backtick. The new qa1f fixture is the qa1b shape rewritten with '~~~' and exercises all three tilde-only paths in one document: the opener (whose info string CONTAINS a backtick, which would disqualify a backtick opener), the mismatched closer (a backtick run does NOT close a tilde fence) and the tilde closer. That takes bash 181 -> 186 and the PS QA-1 row set 26 -> 31. It needs no host qualifier: no case is conditional on any host capability except the BC-19 unreadable-file row, which is skipped only when running as root (uid 0) - the captured run was uid 1000. CORPUS FLOOR (do NOT re-baseline it upward): AC-15 walks the LIVE docs/features/_archived/ corpus, which GROWS by one section every time a task archives - this task's own stage-7 archive takes it from 34 to 35. So AC-15's hard row is corpus_dirty == 0 (the property AC-15 actually states) and the other two rows are FLOORS, >= 34 clean and >= 3 terminal-footer, being the figures measured on the run that set 152 and RE-MEASURED unchanged at 34/0/3 on the run that set 181 and again, read-only in a sandbox, on the run that set 186 (41 archived delivery docs, 34 clean, 0 dirty, 3 footer-bearing, 7 with no heading). Raising a floor to match a grown corpus re-opens the same trap one commit later; the floors still discriminate because corpus_clean sits EXACTLY on 34, so any section that stops classifying cleanly drops it to 33 AND trips corpus_dirty. Proven by mutation in a scratch corpus copy, not by argument: removing one clean section -> 33, red; making one section unaccounted -> 33 + dirty 1, both rows red; adding a 35th clean section -> all three rows still green. Both twins parse the tally line STRICTLY (bash: a guarded ${line##*...} plus a ^[0-9]+$ test; PS: -gt 0, not -ne 0 against the -1 sentinel), because the pre-change script prints NO tally line and an unguarded parse counts every unmeasured section as footer-bearing - which handed the >= 3 floor a spurious green against the very script it exists to detect. With the strict parse the anti-revert split was unchanged from round 1 at 70/82 - a ROUND-2 figure, over the then-152-row set, SUPERSEDED: the current split is 84/102, see ANTI-REVERT EVIDENCE below - and all three AC-15 rows are red against the pre-change script. ANTI-REVERT EVIDENCE, captured not derived: the same 186-row driver driven against the COMMITTED pre-change script (`git show HEAD:.harness/scripts/archive-task.sh`, sha256 f43f549924cc0f0ae885868b5b1577774753d02eb83e0a2d840440897a74f281, extracted to a scratch path and passed through the driver's optional [archive-task-path] argument) scores PASS: 84 / FAIL: 102, i.e. 102 of the 186 rows are load-bearing. Round history, each figure captured on its own run and none of the earlier ones current: round 1/2 70/82 over 152 rows; round 3 82/99 over 181 rows (the 29 rows it added split 12 green / 17 red, because the pre-change script harvested BOTH sections correctly - it is the CORRECT reference on the multi-section fixture, so only the fenced-heading and refusal rows are new coverage against it); round 4 84/102 over 186 rows (the 5 rows it added split 2 green / 3 red - the pre-change script exits 0 and does harvest the real entry, but it prints no tally line, writes the tilde-quoted documentation bullet into the index and prints no 'Quoted headings:' line). The split is corroborated at the LABEL level, never by totals: 186 post-PASS labels, all unique; 84 pre-PASS + 102 pre-FAIL = 186, all unique; the pre-change run's stderr 'Failures:' header is followed by exactly 102 label lines (CR-8: count the labels, not the header); `comm` between the two sets empty in BOTH directions; pre-PASS and pre-FAIL disjoint. A total can stay put while coverage moves - that was round 2's lesson and it is why the label sets, not the counts, are the instrument. Other captured bash runs in the same tree: verify_all 32/0/0 (check count unchanged at 32 - I.4 gained a condition and kept its id, no step call added or removed); sync-self --check exit 0 with both archive-task copies changed. There is deliberately NO test_archive_task_ps_assertions key: pwsh is not installed on this host (`command -v pwsh` fails), so archive-task.ps1, verify_all.ps1's I.4 arm and test-archive-task.ps1 are green-by-symmetry ONLY and no real tally exists.
